subproblem.title: Orthonormal basis of ℝ^P adapted to the splitting V ⊕ V^⊥
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) with orthogonal complement V^⊥. Then there is an orthonormal basis e_0, …, e_{P−1} of ℝ^P, indexed by Fin P, such that for every i ∈ Fin P either e_i ∈ V or e_i ∈ V^⊥.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), ∃ e : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P), ∀ i : Fin P, e i ∈ V ∨ e i ∈ Vᗮ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (an adapted orthonormal basis, obtained by concatenating orthonormal bases of V and V^⊥ using ℝ^P = V ⊕ V^⊥ orthogonally). The parent's later steps only use the dichotomy 'e_i ∈ V or e_i ∈ V^⊥', so the ordering 'the first r = dim V vectors lie in V' is not recorded.
1. (V and V^⊥ are orthogonal.) If v ∈ V and w ∈ V^⊥ then ⟨v, w⟩ = 0, by definition of V^⊥. In particular V ∩ V^⊥ = {0}, because a vector in both is orthogonal to itself.
2. (V + V^⊥ = ℝ^P.) Let x be orthogonal to the subspace V + V^⊥.
   - Since V ⊆ V + V^⊥, x is orthogonal to V, i.e. x ∈ V^⊥.
   - Since V^⊥ ⊆ V + V^⊥, x is orthogonal to V^⊥, i.e. x ∈ (V^⊥)^⊥.
   - Hence ⟨x, x⟩ = 0 (x ∈ V^⊥ and x is orthogonal to every vector of V^⊥), so x = 0.
   Thus (V + V^⊥)^⊥ = {0}. Since ℝ^P is finite-dimensional, V + V^⊥ = ((V + V^⊥)^⊥)^⊥ = ℝ^P. With step 1, ℝ^P is the internal orthogonal direct sum of V and V^⊥.
3. (Concatenate.) Choose an orthonormal basis f_1, …, f_r of V and an orthonormal basis h_1, …, h_s of V^⊥; finite-dimensional inner product spaces have orthonormal bases.
   - The concatenated family (f_1, …, f_r, h_1, …, h_s) is orthonormal: within each block by choice, and ⟨f_j, h_l⟩ = 0 by step 1.
   - It spans V + V^⊥ = ℝ^P by step 2.
   - An orthonormal family is linearly independent, so it is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P. In particular r + s = P.
4. (Re-index.) The index set {1, …, r} ⊔ {1, …, s} has P elements. Transport the basis along a bijection with Fin P and call the result e = (e_i)_{i ∈ Fin P}. Its vectors are the f_j ∈ V and the h_l ∈ V^⊥, so each e_i lies in V or in V^⊥. ∎
Formalization note (Mathlib): this is DirectSum.IsInternal.subordinateOrthonormalBasis for the Bool-indexed family b ↦ cond b V Vᗮ.
- The family is orthogonal by Submodule.orthogonalFamily_self.
- It is internal by OrthogonalFamily.isInternal_iff: internal ⟺ (⨆ b, cond b V Vᗮ)ᗮ = ⊥, which is step 2 via Submodule.orthogonal_le, le_iSup and Submodule.orthogonal_disjoint.
- The dimension is finrank_euclideanSpace_fin.
- DirectSum.IsInternal.subordinateOrthonormalBasis_subordinate places each basis vector in cond b V Vᗮ, where b = subordinateOrthonormalBasisIndex. Generalize this index and case on b.
The following script compiled in scratch for exactly this frozen type, after import GMT.Ch07.Submission in the contract scope, with default options and axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]:
  intro P V
  have hW' : OrthogonalFamily ℝ (fun b : Bool => ↥(cond b V Vᗮ)) fun b => (cond b V Vᗮ).subtypeₗᵢ :=
    V.orthogonalFamily_self
  have hW : DirectSum.IsInternal fun b : Bool => cond b V Vᗮ := by
    rw [hW'.isInternal_iff]
    rw [Submodule.eq_bot_iff]
    intro x hx
    have h1 : x ∈ Vᗮ := Submodule.orthogonal_le (le_iSup (fun b : Bool => cond b V Vᗮ) true) hx
    have h2 : x ∈ Vᗮᗮ := Submodule.orthogonal_le (le_iSup (fun b : Bool => cond b V Vᗮ) false) hx
    exact Submodule.mem_bot ℝ |>.mp (by
      have := Submodule.orthogonal_disjoint Vᗮ
      exact (Submodule.disjoint_def.mp this) x h1 h2 ▸ Submodule.zero_mem _)
  refine ⟨hW.subordinateOrthonormalBasis (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) hW', fun i => ?_⟩
  have hmem := hW.subordinateOrthonormalBasis_subordinate (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) i hW'
  revert hmem
  generalize hW.subordinateOrthonormalBasisIndex (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) i hW' = b
  cases b
  · intro hmem
    exact Or.inr hmem
  · intro hmem
    exact Or.inl hmem
proof_key_steps: V and V^⊥ are orthogonal, and V + V^⊥ = ℝ^P because a vector orthogonal to both is orthogonal to itself.
Concatenating orthonormal bases of V and V^⊥ gives an orthonormal family that spans ℝ^P, hence an orthonormal basis with P elements.
Re-index it by Fin P; each basis vector lies in V or in V^⊥.

subproblem.title: The determinant n-covector u ↦ det(⟨g_b, u_a⟩)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and g_0, …, g_{n−1} ∈ ℝ^P. There is an n-covector γ on ℝ^P (a continuous alternating n-linear form, Covector (Euclid P) n) such that γ(u_0, …, u_{n−1}) = det(⟨g_b, u_a⟩)_{a,b ∈ Fin n} for all u_0, …, u_{n−1} ∈ ℝ^P. The matrix has entry ⟨g_b, u_a⟩ in row a and column b; for n = 0 the empty determinant is 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Fin n → Euclid P), ∃ γ : Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ u : Fin n → Euclid P, γ u = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (g b) (u a))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof. There, e'^I(u) := det(⟨u_a, e'_{i_b}⟩) is shown to be an n-covector: row a depends linearly on u_a, the determinant is multilinear and alternating in the rows, and continuity holds in finite dimension. Here the same argument is stated for an arbitrary n-tuple g instead of (e'_{i_0}, …, e'_{i_d}).
1. (Rows.) Let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^n be the linear map L(x) := (⟨g_b, x⟩)_{b ∈ Fin n}; each coordinate x ↦ ⟨g_b, x⟩ is linear. For u ∈ (ℝ^P)^n, the matrix (⟨g_b, u_a⟩)_{a,b} is the matrix whose row a is L(u_a).
2. (Row determinant.) Regard the determinant as a function of the n rows: D(r_0, …, r_{n−1}) := det(matrix with rows r_a). D is multilinear (linear in each row) and alternating (zero when two rows coincide). In Mathlib this is Matrix.detRowAlternating.
3. (Multilinear and alternating.) Define γ_0(u) := D(L(u_0), …, L(u_{n−1})) = det(⟨g_b, u_a⟩)_{a,b}.
   - γ_0 is linear in each argument u_a, because L is linear and D is linear in each row.
   - If u_a = u_{a'} for some a ≠ a', then L(u_a) = L(u_{a'}), so two rows coincide and γ_0(u) = 0.
   Hence γ_0 is an alternating n-linear map. In Mathlib it is AlternatingMap.compLinearMap of detRowAlternating with LinearMap.pi (fun b => innerₛₗ ℝ (g b)), and its value at u is definitionally det(Matrix.of fun a b => ⟨g_b, u_a⟩).
4. (Continuity.) Each entry u ↦ ⟨g_b, u_a⟩ is continuous: a coordinate projection followed by the continuous inner product. The determinant is a polynomial in the n² entries. Therefore u ↦ det(⟨g_b, u_a⟩) is continuous on (ℝ^P)^n (fun_prop, or Continuous.matrix_det).
5. (Package.) A multilinear alternating map that is continuous is a continuous alternating map. Combine:
   - the continuous multilinear map ⟨γ_0 as a multilinear map, continuity from step 4⟩, and
   - the alternating property from step 3.
   The resulting γ : Covector (Euclid P) n satisfies γ(u) = γ_0(u) = det(⟨g_b, u_a⟩)_{a,b} for all u. The argument is uniform in n: for n = 0 the empty determinant is 1 and γ is the constant 0-covector 1. ∎
Formalization note: the following script compiled in scratch for exactly this frozen type, after import GMT.Ch07.Submission in the contract scope, with default options and axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]:
  intro P n g
  let f : Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ :=
    Matrix.detRowAlternating.compLinearMap (LinearMap.pi fun b => innerₛₗ ℝ (g b))
  have hf : ∀ u, f u = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (g b) (u a)) := by
    intro u
    rfl
  have hc : Continuous fun u : Fin n → Euclid P => Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (g b) (u a)) := by
    fun_prop
  refine ⟨⟨⟨f.toMultilinearMap, ?_⟩, f.map_eq_zero_of_eq'⟩, ?_⟩
  · exact hc.congr fun u => (hf u).symm
  · intro u
    exact hf u
proof_key_steps: Row a of the matrix (⟨g_b,u_a⟩)_{a,b} is L(u_a), where L(x) = (⟨g_b,x⟩)_b is linear.
The row determinant is multilinear and alternating, so u ↦ det(⟨g_b,u_a⟩) is an alternating n-linear map.
It is continuous (a polynomial in continuous entries), hence a continuous alternating map, i.e. an n-covector.

audit.reason: The exact type specifies the stated row/column convention for arbitrary P, n and g. Composing the row determinant with the linear coordinate map proves alternation and multilinearity; continuity follows from the continuous entries and determinant polynomial. The empty determinant case is covered. No parent or sibling result is assumed.

subproblem.title: n!·β(u) as the sum of β(e_I)·det(⟨e_{I(b)}, u_a⟩) over all index maps I
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let e_0, …, e_{P−1} be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (indexed by Fin P), let β be an n-covector on ℝ^P and let u = (u_0, …, u_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n. Then n!·β(u) = Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} β(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) · det(⟨e_{I(b)}, u_a⟩)_{a,b ∈ Fin n}. The sum runs over all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and the matrix has entry ⟨e_{I(b)}, u_a⟩ in row a and column b.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (e : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)) (β : Covector (Euclid P) n) (u : Fin n → Euclid P), (n.factorial : ℝ) * β u = ∑ I : Fin n → Fin P, β (fun a => e (I a)) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (e (I b)) (u a))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof. There, β = Σ_I β(e'_I)·e'^I is proved by expanding each argument u_a = Σ_m⟨u_a, e'_m⟩e'_m and using that β is alternating. Here the sum is taken over all index maps I : Fin n → Fin P instead of strictly increasing ones. The two forms agree:
- a non-injective I contributes 0, since its determinant has two equal columns;
- each strictly increasing J occurs exactly n! times as J∘π, π a permutation, and β(e_{J∘π})·det(⟨e_{J(π b)}, u_a⟩) = sign(π)²·β(e_J)·det(⟨e_{J(b)}, u_a⟩) = β(e_J)·det(⟨e_{J(b)}, u_a⟩).
This explains the factor n!. The proof below proves the stated identity directly. Write e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
1. (Multilinear expansion.) For every v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n, β(v) = Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_{a ∈ Fin n} ⟨e_{I(a)}, v_a⟩) · β(e_I).
   - Since e is orthonormal, v_a = Σ_{m ∈ Fin P} ⟨e_m, v_a⟩ e_m for each a (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr').
   - Expanding β multilinearly in all n arguments (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_sum) gives β(v) = Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} β(⟨e_{I(0)}, v_0⟩ e_{I(0)}, …, ⟨e_{I(n−1)}, v_{n−1}⟩ e_{I(n−1)}).
   - Pulling the scalars out of every argument (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ) turns each term into (Π_a ⟨e_{I(a)}, v_a⟩)·β(e_I).
2. (Alternation.) For each permutation σ of Fin n, β(u∘σ) = sign(σ)·β(u), because β is alternating (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to β.toAlternatingMap). Since sign(σ) = ±1, sign(σ)·β(u∘σ) = sign(σ)²·β(u) = β(u). Fin n has n! permutations (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin), so summing over them gives n!·β(u) = Σ_σ sign(σ)·β(u∘σ).
3. (Substitute and exchange sums.) Apply step 1 with v := u∘σ, only to the term β(u∘σ) and not again to β(e_I). This gives
   n!·β(u) = Σ_σ Σ_I sign(σ)·(Π_a ⟨e_{I(a)}, u_{σ(a)}⟩)·β(e_I).
   Exchanging the two finite sums (Finset.sum_comm) and factoring out β(e_I):
   n!·β(u) = Σ_I β(e_I)·Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_a ⟨e_{I(a)}, u_{σ(a)}⟩.
4. (Leibniz formula.) For fixed I let M^I be the n×n matrix with M^I_{a,b} := ⟨e_{I(b)}, u_a⟩. The Leibniz formula det M = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b M_{σ(b), b} (Matrix.det_apply') gives det M^I = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b ⟨e_{I(b)}, u_{σ(b)}⟩. This is the inner sum of step 3 with the product variable renamed from a to b. Therefore n!·β(u) = Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} β(e_I)·det(⟨e_{I(b)}, u_a⟩)_{a,b}.
   The argument is valid for every n, including n = 0 (0! = 1, a single empty map I, empty determinant 1) and P = 0. ∎

subproblem.title: Laplace expansion along column k writes a determinant covector in the form w♭∧α with w = g_k
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, g_0, …, g_d ∈ ℝ^P and k ∈ Fin n. Let γ be an n-covector on ℝ^P with γ(u) = det(⟨g_b, u_a⟩)_{a,b ∈ Fin n} for all u ∈ (ℝ^P)^n (entry ⟨g_b, u_a⟩ in row a, column b). Then there is a d-covector α on ℝ^P such that, for all u = (u_0, …, u_d), γ(u) = Σ_{i=0}^{d} (−1)^i ⟨g_k, u_i⟩ α(u_0, …, û_i, …, u_d). Here (u_0, …, û_i, …, u_d) = removeNth i u is u with the i-th entry deleted.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (g : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P) (k : Fin (d + 1)) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1)), (∀ u : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, γ u = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (g b) (u a))) → ∃ α : Covector (Euclid P) d, ∀ u : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, γ u = ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (inner ℝ (g k) (u i) * α (i.removeNth u))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof. There, det(⟨u_a, e'_{i_b}⟩) is expanded along column k (Matrix.det_succ_column), with α := (−1)^k·e'^{I∖i_k} built as in step 2 from the d-tuple obtained by deleting the k-th vector. Here the same argument is stated for an arbitrary (d+1)-tuple g.
1. (The minor covector.) Let g' : Fin d → ℝ^P, g'_{b'} := g_{k.succAbove b'}, be g with its k-th entry deleted; k.succAbove : Fin d → Fin (d+1) is the increasing map whose image is Fin (d+1) ∖ {k}. By the sibling lemma det_covector with n := d and the tuple g', there is a d-covector γ' with γ'(v) = det(⟨g'_{b'}, v_{a'}⟩)_{a',b' ∈ Fin d} for all v ∈ (ℝ^P)^d. Put α := (−1)^k · γ'; a scalar multiple of a d-covector is a d-covector.
2. (Laplace expansion.) Fix u ∈ (ℝ^P)^{d+1} and let M be the (d+1)×(d+1) real matrix M_{a,b} := ⟨g_b, u_a⟩, so γ(u) = det M by hypothesis. Laplace expansion along column k (Matrix.det_succ_column) gives
   det M = Σ_{i ∈ Fin(d+1)} (−1)^{i+k} · M_{i,k} · det(M^{(i,k)}),
   where M^{(i,k)} := M.submatrix i.succAbove k.succAbove is M with row i and column k removed.
3. (Identify the terms.)
   - M_{i,k} = ⟨g_k, u_i⟩.
   - The (a', b') entry of M^{(i,k)} is M_{i.succAbove a', k.succAbove b'} = ⟨g_{k.succAbove b'}, u_{i.succAbove a'}⟩ = ⟨g'_{b'}, (removeNth i u)_{a'}⟩, because (removeNth i u)_{a'} = u_{i.succAbove a'} by definition of Fin.removeNth.
   - Therefore M^{(i,k)} is the matrix (⟨g'_{b'}, (removeNth i u)_{a'}⟩)_{a',b'}, and det(M^{(i,k)}) = γ'(removeNth i u) by step 1.
4. (Signs.) Since (−1)^{i+k} = (−1)^i (−1)^k and real multiplication is commutative,
   (−1)^{i+k} ⟨g_k, u_i⟩ γ'(removeNth i u) = (−1)^i (⟨g_k, u_i⟩ · ((−1)^k γ'(removeNth i u))) = (−1)^i (⟨g_k, u_i⟩ · α(removeNth i u)).
   Summing over i gives γ(u) = Σ_{i=0}^{d} (−1)^i ⟨g_k, u_i⟩ α(removeNth i u) for every u, as claimed.
   Check for d = 0: k = 0, γ' is the constant 0-covector 1 and α = 1, so the formula reads γ(u) = ⟨g_0, u_0⟩, which is the 1×1 determinant. ∎

  obtain ⟨γ', hγ'⟩ := Submission.cbr_ci_cp_pr_inner_det_covector P d (fun b => g (k.succAbove b))

Expand det(⟨g_b,u_a⟩) along column k by Laplace expansion (Matrix.det_succ_column).
The (i,k) minor is the matrix of removeNth i u against g with g_k deleted, so it equals γ'(removeNth i u); regroup (−1)^{i+k} = (−1)^i(−1)^k.
